sections.name: Police: LSPD, sheriff and Highway Patrol
sections.card:
Summary: Three forces chase you. The Los Santos Police Department (LSPD) works inside the city of Los Santos, including its airport and port. The Los Santos County Sheriff's Department (LSSD) also covers Blaine County, and the San Andreas Highway Patrol (SAHP) rides Police Bikes on the highways.
Weak points: Shoot an LSPD officer or sheriff's deputy in the legs and he dies, either straight away or from blood loss. Officers also tend to take cover behind, or stand beside, a burning vehicle that is about to explode.
Tips: The sheriff's deputies drive and fight just like the LSPD, in Sheriff Cruisers.
Tips: Once you fire a weapon or reach two stars, Highway Patrol officers open up on you with Pistols. Officers who spawned on a bike follow you on it; those who spawned on foot stay on foot, though they may grab civilian cars.

sections.name: Police at one and two stars
sections.card:
Summary: At one star officers, soldiers and security guards chase you, and police and soldiers try to arrest you at gunpoint. At two stars police shoot to kill, drive much more aggressively to ram you off the road, and at least three police cars chase you.
Weak points: At one star the police only hold you at gunpoint, and fighting back or running away raises it to two stars at once. Security guards and police on motorcycles open fire straight away instead of arresting you.
Tips: At two stars some police cars sit by the road waiting for you to drive past, and others mix into normal traffic with lights and sirens switched off until you get close.
Tips: The police only try to arrest you in a vehicle if you stop the car after about a minute of being chased without hurting a single cop.

sections.name: Police at three stars
sections.card:
Summary: Three stars brings roadblocks of police cars and police transporters, sometimes with a spike strip put down behind them. A Police Maverick helicopter also follows you overhead, with NOOSE TRU officers aboard.
Weak points: The helicopter hangs around until every rifleman aboard is dead, then flies back to base, though a new one soon takes its place. At night its spotlight points out your position to the ground units.
Tips: Every officer who spawns at three stars or more wears a bulletproof vest, and officers run up to a car you have stopped in, drag you out and kill you on the spot, so keep moving.

sections.name: NOOSE TRU at four and five stars
sections.card:
Summary: At four stars NOOSE TRU teams come to kill you, three officers to a vehicle, in FIB Grangers in Los Santos or Sheriff SUVs in Blaine County, with two hanging off the sides firing at you while more shoot from Police Mavericks overhead. At five stars the streets are packed with police and there is hardly any civilian traffic.
Weak points: Their body armour means they take a lot of shots to bring down, but one headshot kills a TRU officer outright, helmet or not, and so does a shot to the legs, at once or through blood loss.
Tips: If you hide in a building or take shelter behind tight cover, they use tear gas to flush you out. A Police Maverick may also drop four officers down by rope, or land and let them out.
Tips: Destroying a Police Maverick that is chasing you can push you up to four stars, but you may have to bring down two or more of them first.

sections.name: Soldiers and Rhino tanks at Fort Zancudo
sections.card:
Summary: Soldiers are never sent to hunt you down, but if a chase passes near Fort Zancudo, soldiers in Crusaders and Barracks join in and try to arrest you. Inside the base they shoot to kill.
Weak points: It blows up after about 3 to 4 tank shells, 5 to 6 RPG shots or 7 to 8 Grenade Launcher shots. A hit on its rear may open the fuel tank, and if you set the trail of fuel alight the tank stops after a few minutes, although its turret still works.
Tips: If you steal an aircraft from the base, or fly one of theirs, soldiers shoot a Rocket Launcher at it. Patrolling Rhinos may also drive out of the base after you, firing their cannons, if you hang around too close for too long.
Tips: Going into the base earns four stars. A flight over it earns two, which quickly turn into four unless you move off fast, and a rocket fired from any aircraft earns five stars at once.

sections.name: Ballas
sections.card:
Summary: A large street gang of African Americans, dressed in purple. They hold nearly all of Davis, where the cul-de-sac of Grove Street is a favorite spot, and they have long been rivals of the Families.
Weak points: You can avoid a fight with them: they usually leave you alone when you simply walk through their territory, and only turn hostile if you taunt them enough, fire a gun there or stand near them and stare.
Tips: Once they turn hostile they shoot, stab or punch you, and their dogs sometimes attack too.
Tips: Starting a gunfight with a gang, or killing several of its members in a row, gives you two stars.

sections.name: The Lost MC
sections.card:
Summary: A biker gang. Its Los Santos chapter is mostly seen in East Vinewood, where members patrol in Gang Burritos and keep a clubhouse; a hideout was set up in Stab City.
Tips: After the main story you can still meet them at their East Vinewood clubhouse, Hookies in North Chumash, R L Hunter & Sons in Grapeseed and Stab City.
Tips: Lost MC members who spot Trevor attack him at once.

sections.name: Sharks
sections.card:
Summary: Sharks in GTA V are quick and deadly, and they often go for you as soon as they see you. They turn up more at night, appear on the minimap as a red dot, and circle you for a while before striking. Now and then there are two.
Weak points: One shot from a boat kills a shark, so keep watch and shoot any you see from the surface before you go under. A boat or Submersible rammed into one also kills it, and stabbing it again and again with a knife works but is extremely hard.
Tips: A single bite is enough to kill you, even at full health and armor. If you are too deep or too far out to reach your boat or the shore, head into sunken plane or ship ruins: the shark often swims off.
Tips: The PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One versions also have Hammerhead Sharks, which never attack. If you get to the end of the map, the game scripts a shark to show up and kill you.

sections.name: Cougars
sections.card:
Summary: Big wild cats that live in the forests and hills of San Andreas, from the Vinewood Hills up to Mount Chiliad. A loud growl often gives a cougar away first; then it charges relentlessly, pounces and kills you at once with a bite to the throat.
Weak points: Cougars flee if you drive or fire a weapon, and they leave you alone while you stand on top of a vehicle. A quick player can also kick one to kill it or knock it out.
Tips: Trevor's special ability lets him survive a cougar attack with no damage.
Tips: In the Hunting side activity cougars turn up a lot. Like deer, they show as a red circle on the map, which can easily lead you straight into an attack.

sections.name: Body Armor
sections.card:
Summary: A protective blue vest in five tiers, all bought from Ammu-Nation: Super Light (20%) for $500, Light (40%) for $1,000, Standard (60%) for $1,500, Heavy (80%) for $2,000 and Super Heavy (100%) for $2,500.
Uses: Armor pads your health against gunfire, explosions and fire, and in GTA V it also protects you from falls and impacts again. Each tier adds another 20%.
Tips: Climbing into a Police Riot gives you armor. It shows as a blue bar next to your health bar below the radar.

sections.name: Health, snacks and vending machines
sections.card:
Summary: Your health comes back on its own only up to the halfway mark: if it drops below 50%, standing still, without walking or running, lets it climb back to 50%.
Uses: Snacks from convenience stores heal you and are eaten as you buy them: P’s & Q’s cost $1, EgoChaser $2 and Meteorite Bar $4, and each heals a different amount. Sprunk or eCola from a vending machine costs $1.
Tips: You can also shoplift snacks, and dead enemies and pedestrians can drop them. Vending machines never show on the map.
Tips: In GTA V you cannot buy food from street vendors or restaurants; the only food you can buy is snacks from convenience stores.

sections.name: Parachute
sections.card:
Summary: A $100 parachute from Ammu-Nation, unlocked after the mission Minor Turbulence; getting into any aircraft also gives you one.
Uses: Once the chute is open you can fire one-handed weapons, which means handguns and one-handed submachine guns. You can also open it from a bike that is falling, but you are ejected and the bike drops on its own.
Tips: Pull back on the movement stick to land safely: pushing forward makes you faceplant, which may injure or kill you.
Tips: The chute is vulnerable to gunfire and to nearby explosions that set it on fire, and a ripped chute detaches and sends you falling.

sections.name: Rhino Tank
sections.card:
Summary: A battle tank that weighs 60 tons and carries a 120mm cannon. Warstock Cache & Carry sells it for $3,000,000 and it then waits in your aircraft hangar; you can also steal one at Fort Zancudo.
Uses: The cannon shoots once every 1.5 seconds with a range of 190 meters, and it works well against nearly everything. Its tracks flatten small vehicles, which blow up or burn, and you are hard to bust while inside.
Tips: Keep the cannon off close targets in tight spaces such as alleyways, because the shell can explode right beside the tank and damage it.
Tips: Because the gun is solid, things like light poles, traffic lights and walls can get in the way of your aim and may even leave you stuck.

sections.name: Stun Gun
sections.card:
Summary: A Coil handgun that fires a single probe to stun a target. You get it in the mission Monkey Business, and afterwards you can buy it at Ammu-Nation for $100.
Uses: A stunned person drops and cannot get up, and usually dies, though street criminals and animals sometimes get back up as though nothing had happened. A shot to the head puts them down at once, and someone in a vehicle has a good chance of falling out.
Tips: Its range is short, only a little more than most melee weapons. It is classed as a handgun, so you can use it in drive-bys, though damage and fire rate are low. It can also shoot out the tires of vehicles that are not bulletproof, and it can kill people.

sections.name: Sticky Bombs
sections.card:
Summary: A throwable explosive that sticks to any surface it hits, vehicles included, and goes off whenever you choose. It costs $400 and is unlocked by the mission Friends Reunited.
Uses: A sticky bomb attaches to any vehicle and goes off whenever you choose, a bit like a landmine. In story mode it will not stick to pedestrians. Three of them are enough to destroy a Rhino in free roam.
Tips: Keep your own car out of the blast radius, because shooting a placed bomb sets it off, and so does ramming one stuck to a vertical surface.
Tips: You can have 20 placed at once, the 21st removes the first, and they never explode on their own.
